stem: An application generates thousands of small log records every hour that must land in an S3 bucket for later analytics, and per-request charges are the largest line item on the storage bill.

choices.text: Group the records into fewer, larger objects, or use S3 Batch Operations, before uploading
Add an S3 Lifecycle rule that transitions the objects to a colder storage class
Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering on the bucket
Turn on S3 Transfer Acceleration for the uploads

rationale: Grouping the small records into fewer, larger objects, or running the copy through S3 Batch Operations, cuts the per-request PUT charges that are driving the bill, because S3 bills each PUT, COPY, POST, and DELETE individually. A Lifecycle rule that transitions objects to a colder class lowers the per-GB storage rate over time, but it does nothing about the request charges generated by thousands of individual uploads. Intelligent-Tiering changes the storage-class cost of objects already sitting in the bucket; it has no effect on how many requests the upload itself generates. Transfer Acceleration speeds up transfer over long distances using edge locations, which is a latency feature, not a request-count reduction.
